    elif tok.startswith('repo/'):
        f=pathlib.Path('repo')/tok[len('repo/'):]

    n=len(f.read_text(errors='replace').splitlines())
    if int(a)<1 or int(b or a)>n or int(a)>int(b or a): bad.append(('range',tok,a,b,n))
print("bad:", bad)
print("bytes:", len(text.encode()))

     2	title: "Agent runtime architecture"
     3	summary: "How OpenClaw structures the built-in agent runtime: code layout, boundaries, resource manifests, and runtime selection."
     4	---
     5	
     6	OpenClaw owns the built-in agent runtime. Runtime code lives under `src/agents/`, model/provider transport lives under `src/llm/`, and `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` barrels expose the plugin-facing contracts.
     7	
     8	## Runtime Layout
     9	
    10	| Path                                | Owns                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
    11	| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    12	| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/` | Built-in attempt loop (`run.ts`, `run/`), model selection and provider normalization (`model*.ts`), per-provider request params (`extra-params.*`), compaction, transcript and session wiring.                            |
    13	| `src/agents/sessions/`              | Session persistence (`session-manager.ts`), resource discovery (`package-manager.ts`, `resource-loader.ts`), in-session `extensions` loading, prompt templates, skills, themes, and TUI-backed tool renderers (`tools/`). |
    14	| `packages/agent-core/`              | Reusable agent core (`@openclaw/agent-core`): agent loop, harness types, messages, compaction helpers, prompt templates, skills, and session storage contracts.                                                           |
    15	| `src/agents/runtime/`               | OpenClaw facade that wires `@openclaw/agent-core` to the plugin SDK LLM runtime and re-exports it plus local proxy utilities.                                                                                             |
    16	| `src/agents/agent-tools*.ts`        | OpenClaw-owned tool definitions, parameter schemas, tool policy, before/after tool-call adapters, and host/sandbox edit tools.                                                                                            |
    17	| `src/agents/agent-hooks/`           | Built-in runtime hooks: compaction safeguard, compaction instructions, context pruning.                                                                                                                                   |
    18	| `src/agents/harness/`               | Harness registry, selection policy, and lifecycle for the built-in and plugin-registered harnesses.                                                                                                                       |
    19	| `src/llm/`                          | Model/provider registry, transport helpers, and provider-specific stream implementations (`src/llm/providers/`).                                                                                                          |
    20	
    21	## Boundaries
    22	
    23	Core calls the built-in runtime through OpenClaw modules and SDK barrels. No external agent framework packages remain. Plugins use documented `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` entrypoints and do not import `src/**` internals.
    24	
    25	`@earendil-works/pi-tui` remains a third-party dependency: a terminal component toolkit used by the local TUI and session tool renderers. Internalizing it would be a separate vendoring effort.
    26	
    27	## Streaming update ownership
    28	
    29	Assistant `message_update` envelopes reconstructed from partial-free text deltas
    30	are shallow-frozen and shared with the loop's current message. Later deltas create
    31	new envelopes, preserving retained earlier text snapshots. Nested metadata is not
    32	deep-frozen. Listeners should read updates and keep their own derived state;
    33	terminal-message hooks retain their existing mutation behavior.
    34	
    35	Provider-owned partial snapshots remain mutable while streaming. Agent-core
    36	copies their top-level envelope before publication so retained updates preserve
    37	references when a provider replaces fields such as `content` or `usage`.
    38	
    39	## Manifests
    40	
    41	Resource packages declare OpenClaw resources in `package.json` metadata. Entries are file paths or globs relative to the package root:
    42	
    43	```json
    44	{
    45	  "openclaw": {
    46	    "extensions": ["extensions/index.ts"],
    47	    "skills": ["skills/*.md"],
    48	    "prompts": ["prompts/*.md"],
    49	    "themes": ["themes/*.json"]
    50	  }
    51	}
    52	```
    53	
    54	Resource types not listed in a manifest fall back to discovery of conventional `extensions/`, `skills/`, `prompts/`, and `themes/` directories.
    55	
    56	## Runtime Selection
    57	
    58	- The built-in runtime id is `openclaw`. The legacy alias `pi` normalizes to `openclaw`. The alias `codex-app-server` normalizes to `codex`.
    59	- Plugin harnesses register additional runtime ids (for example `codex`).
    60	- Runtime policy is model/provider-scoped `agentRuntime.id` config (model entry wins over provider entry). Unset or `default` resolves to `auto`.
    61	- `auto` selects a registered plugin harness that supports the effective provider route, otherwise the built-in OpenClaw runtime. A provider or model prefix alone never selects a harness.
    62	- OpenAI may select `codex` implicitly. This happens only for an exact official HTTPS Platform Responses or ChatGPT Responses route with no authored request override. Completions adapters, custom endpoints, and routes with authored request behavior stay on `openclaw`. Plaintext official HTTP endpoints are rejected. See [OpenAI implicit agent runtime](/providers/openai/runtimes#implicit-agent-runtime).
    63	
    64	## Model Runtime Generations
    65	
    66	Gateway startup and config, plugin, or auth publication build one prepared model runtime generation per configured agent. Each generation owns the discovered auth template, model registry, and projected model catalog as one atomic snapshot. Agent runs fork mutable auth and registry stores from that snapshot. Browse, status, cron, doctor, TUI, PDF, and image paths read the published catalog instead of repeating filesystem discovery.
    67	
    68	Standalone embedded runtimes publish the same snapshot shape at their activation boundary. A failed or stale generation is never served alongside a newer partial generation. The lifecycle owner must publish a complete replacement first.
    69	
    70	Runtime selections resolve in the requesting agent's scope before becoming owner keys. Lease admission carries that prepared choice forward and reads the exact owner's snapshot. Retries must observe a changed owner or publication gate; unchanged publication state fails with a retryable error instead of blocking the Gateway event loop.
    71	
    72	If publication supersedes unfinished run preparation, admission prepares again on the current generation once before reporting a retryable error. A reply whose captured dispatch generation was replaced can also discard that initial selection before execution and enter current admission. These retries do not replay model requests or tools. Once execution begins, nested work stays pinned to its admitted generation; changing plugin owners at that point could mix callbacks and resources from different generations.
    73	
    74	Auth-triggered publication allows up to two fresh-generation retries for supersession. Exhaustion remains a typed, retryable error, and a later request can recover the configured owner through normal catalog recovery. Other lifecycle failures retain their existing single fresh-generation retry.
    75	
    76	## Compute workers
    77	
    78	Code-mode execution, compaction planning, and file-tool planning use the reusable `WorkerTaskPool`.
    79	Its scheduler and task protocol live in the private `@openclaw/worker-runtime`
    80	package. The OpenClaw host adapter owns native worker creation, resource custody,
    81	and process accounting. Plugins use the public
    82	[worker SDK entrypoints](/plugins/sdk-overview/infrastructure#worker-task-admission).
    83	
    84	The package keeps task results, execution settlement, and resource release as

5:## Context-window economics and cache stability
6:Unchanged prefixes (instructions, tools, context) are cached; model/effort/tool/image changes break reuse (`pages/reference/prompt-caching.md:10-38`, `pages/reference/prompt-caching.md:260-272`). `cacheRetention`: 5-min/1-h, writes 1.25x/2x input, reads 0.1x; `long` = 1.6x `short` (`derived`); `cache-ttl` prunes stale results (`pages/reference/prompt-caching.md:193-270`).
8:## Queue steering and backpressure
9:`steer` default injects during tools; running tools are never interrupted, parallel batches never skipped. Modes `steer`/`followup`/`collect`/`interrupt`: `collect` coalesces, `interrupt` aborts (`pages/concepts/queue-steering.md:11-125`).
11:## Rate limiting and burst behavior
12:Limits: 128 unauth handshakes/IP, auth 10/60s + 5-min lockout, webhook 20/60s + 60s, writes 30/60s/method, ACP 120/10s, restart 30s (`pages/gateway/security/rate-limiting.md:17-25`). Overflow `503` with no `Retry-After`; tune via `OPENCLAW_MAX_PREAUTH_CONNECTIONS_PER_IP` and `gateway.auth.rateLimit` (`pages/gateway/security/rate-limiting.md:29-125`).

40:Rate limits: 16 attempts (15 retries, `derived`) per outage; backoff 1 s to 60 s (30 s others); SDK waits cap 60 s; cooldowns 30 s → 1 min → 5 min (`pages/concepts/model-failover.md:401-496`). Fallback sticky 10 min idle capped 30 min; `timeoutSeconds` per attempt, idle 120 s cloud / 300 s self-hosted, 2× progress (`pages/concepts/model-failover.md:437-494`, `pages/concepts/agent-loop.md:311-312`).

43:DB access uses workers via a SQLite writer broker, never the main thread; admission follows each worker's ordered cursor over two writer isolates (`pages/reference/database-schemas/worker-access.md:49-170`). `runSqliteImmediateTransaction` retries preparation via `busy_timeout` (not a total deadline), never replays a commit; UI reads use two-task-per-reader headroom (`pages/plugins/sdk-overview/infrastructure.md:170-190`, `pages/reference/database-schemas/worker-access.md:247-252`).
